QuestionStmt.S: The solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt AX is $4.9 \times 10^{-13}$. What is its solubility in mol·dm$^{-3}$?

Solution.S:
For a sparingly soluble salt AX, the dissociation is:

$$AX(s) \rightleftharpoons A^+(aq) + X^-(aq)$$

Let solubility be S mol/dm³. Then at equilibrium:
$$[A^+] = S,\quad [X^-] = S$$

Solubility product:
$$K_{sp} = [A^+][X^-] = S \times S = S^2$$

Given $K_{sp} = 4.9 \times 10^{-13}$:
$$S = \sqrt{4.9 \times 10^{-13}} = \sqrt{49 \times 10^{-14}} = 7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol/dm}^3$$

Thus, the solubility is $7.0 \times 10^{-7}$ mol dm⁻³, which corresponds to option C.
